beats.narration_text: I inherited a regulatory intelligence pipeline that had been quietly dropping real SEC filings — and nobody knew, because it never threw an error.
beats.new_visual_element: A calm dashboard feed — nothing looks wrong

shot.note: Calm feed log — SEC/FINRA/CFTC/FedReg rows ticking in, nothing looks wrong.

beats.narration_text: Five feeds — SEC, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; FINRA, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority; CFTC, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission; and two Federal Register feeds, one filtered for securities and investment filings, the other filtered to CFTC filings — funneled into a scoring and alerting system. Somewhere upstream, a filter checked that every item had a description before letting it through.

shot.note: Diagram: 5 RSS feeds -> normalize -> score -> Postgres -> email alert.

beats.narration_text: Using Claude Code to trace the pipeline node by node, we found a filter silently rejecting any item with an empty description — no log, no error, just gone. Turns out SEC and exchange filings routinely arrive title-only. The filter was treating 'no summary yet' as 'not real.'
beats.new_visual_element: Claude Code diff: the removed empty-description filter

shot.note: Code panel, diff view highlighting the removed empty-description filter.

beats.narration_text: These weren't noise. These were real signal — exchange rule filings, an antitrust case — dropped before a human ever saw them.
beats.new_visual_element: Recovered filings: Cboe, MEMX, Nasdaq GEMX, DOJ antitrust

shot.note: [VERIFY: exact filing citations/URLs before publish — see FACTCHECK.md] List-reveal: Cboe Clear U.S., MEMX LLC, Nasdaq GEMX SRO notice, US v. Edwards LifeSciences.

beats.narration_text: We dropped the filter, re-ran it against the live feeds, and verified the output against the production database. The result: seventy-three additional real items recovered — per run.

shot.note: Before/after count on screen: 297 -> 370 items passed.

beats.narration_text: The sneakiest bugs aren't the ones that crash your pipeline. They're the ones that keep running — and quietly decide what you never get to see.
beats.new_visual_element: Silent filters don't fail loudly — they fail invisibly

shot.note: Statement card: Silent filters don't fail loudly. They fail invisibly.

beats.narration_text: Fixed with Claude Code, verified against live data before it ever touched production.

shot.note: Brand card: @HumanitariansAI, fixed with Claude Code.
